Ask anyone who runs a small office near Trade Street or off SC-14 what changes in April, and the answer is usually the front door. Pollen coats the glass, damp shoes bring in clay, and the entry mat that looked fine all winter is suddenly grey. It is November, which is a good time to plan the spring work, because the schedule is lighter and you can set the routine before the busy months. Here is a practical plan for office cleaning in Greer that carries a business through spring.

What spring does to an office

Winter dirt is mostly salt and dry dust. Spring dirt is wetter and finer. Pollen drifts in through any open door, settles on window sills and desks, and gets pulled into the HVAC when the air conditioning starts working again. At the same time, rain moves clay and grass onto floors, and the entry area takes the brunt. A cleaning plan that was enough in January often leaves a film by May.

The seasonal checklist

  • Entry glass cleaned inside and out, including the door frame and handles
  • Entry mats shaken, vacuumed or replaced, and the floor beneath them washed
  • Window sills, blinds and tracks wiped of pollen
  • Air vents and return grilles dusted where they are reachable
  • Carpet traffic lanes vacuumed more slowly, in two directions
  • Restroom grout, fixtures and floors detailed
  • Break room fridge, microwave and sink given a deeper wipe than the weekly routine
  • Light switches, keypads and railings disinfected

This list goes beyond the usual weekly tasks, which are desks, counters, restrooms, trash and floors. We usually schedule the seasonal items as a one-time deep visit, then return to the normal rhythm.

The split helps keep the regular price steady, because the deeper work is scheduled separately rather than folded into every visit.

Small habits that help between visits

The cleaning team can only do so much if the office works against it. A few small habits reduce what pollen and clay bring in, and they cost nothing.

  • Keep exterior doors closed when you can, and prop them open only for deliveries.
  • Use two mats at the main entrance, one outside and one inside, so shoes are wiped twice.
  • Ask staff to leave desks clear at the end of the day so surfaces can be wiped, not just worked around.
  • Replace HVAC filters before pollen season, because clogged filters push fine dust back into the room.
  • Report spills and stains the same day, since fresh marks come out of carpet far more easily.

Offices with clients, such as clinics, salons and studios, may also want an extra focus on waiting areas and restrooms during the spring peak, when visitors arrive with the outside on their shoes. We can add a short mid-week visit for those areas without changing the main schedule.

Planning the calendar

  1. Pick the month you want the deep clean to land, ideally after the heaviest pollen days rather than before.
  2. Decide which days your staff are out or the office is closed, so the team can move furniture.
  3. Choose whether the regular schedule should increase for a few weeks.
  4. Share any quiet-hours rules or building access details at the estimate.
  5. Ask for a follow-up check a few weeks after the deep clean to catch what the pollen brought back.

Finally, think about who else shares the building. If you rent a suite, ask the landlord who cleans the hallways, the shared restroom and the parking-lot entrance, because pollen and clay arrive there first and then walk into your office. Property managers can book a combined visit for common areas and suites. Tell us about it at the estimate, and the team can plan the route so shared spaces are done last, after the suites, when the dust has settled.

A small business owner can also keep a simple log of what was cleaned and when, which helps when staff change or a landlord asks. We are happy to share the checklist we follow, so you can see the tasks listed.

faqs: When should I schedule the spring deep clean?
Many offices pick a date after the heaviest pollen days, which in the Upstate usually means late spring. The estimate visit helps you choose a date that fits your business.
Can the spring clean be done after hours?
Yes. After-hours visits are common for offices, and the schedule is decided during the free in-home estimate.
Do I have to commit to a recurring schedule?
No. You can book a one-time seasonal deep clean, or combine it with daily, weekly or monthly service.
